images.filename: Interiors of Kurumbera fort, West Bengal.jpg
images.caption: Kurumbera fort is located in the village of Gaganeshwar, which is 4 km from Keshiari and 30 km from Kharagpur. According to an Odia inscription at the fort, it was built between 1438 and 1469, during the rule of the Surya Vamsi king of Odisha, Gajapati Kapilendra Dev. However, Kurumbera also has structures built during the Mughal emperor Aurangazeb’s reign (1658-1707) by one Mohammed Tahir, according to another stone inscription.

images.filename: Kurumbera Fort, Gaganeshwar, West Medinipur, West bengal.jpg
images.caption: Kurumbera in local language literary means “stone wall”. Other than the high stone wall surrounding the complex, nothing in the complex looks remotely like part of a fort.  There is a three domes structure inside the complex which appears to be a mosque. The architecture of the surrounding wall clearly shows signs of Odissa temple architecture style. Built during the reign of Gajapati Kapilendra Dev, 1538 – 1469, the structures have been significantly altered during Aurangzeb’s reign (1658-1707) by a local satrap – Mohammad Tahir
